questions.text: Where exactly is the lump located — on the penile shaft, foreskin, glans, or scrotum — and how long have you had it?
questions.purpose: Location and duration guide differential; scrotal lumps have different aetiologies from penile lesions
options: Penile shaft or glans, less than 4 weeks
Penile shaft or glans, more than 4 weeks

questions.text: Is the lump hard, irregular, or fixed (non-mobile)?
questions.purpose: Hard fixed lesions on the penis or testis raise concern for malignancy and require urgent assessment

questions.text: Are there multiple small lumps with a cauliflower-like or wart-like appearance?
questions.purpose: Genital warts (condylomata acuminata) from HPV are the most common genital lumps

questions.text: Has the lump grown rapidly, ulcerated, or bled?
questions.purpose: Rapidly growing or ulcerating penile lesions raise concern for penile carcinoma

questions.text: Have you had recent sexual contact that might put you at risk of an STI?
questions.purpose: STI exposure prompts screening for condyloma, molluscum, or other infectious causes of genital lumps

questions.text: Are you circumcised, and do you have phimosis or difficulty retracting the foreskin?
questions.purpose: Phimosis is a risk factor for penile cancer; foreskin conditions may cause lumps
